First select multiple elements: Shift/Ctrl+click, rubber-band select, or right-click an element → "Select from here FORWARD/BACKWARD in time" (shortcuts ]/[).

The lyrics/chords were replaced — line numbers may have shifted, so clips on the Display track might now show old/wrong content.

Rebuild the Display track from the new text right now (recommended)?
timeline.add_clip.tooltip: Inserts a clip on the Display track at the playhead (or exactly onto a nearby chord-only bar that has no clip yet, if one is close). Faster: right-click directly on an empty spot on the Display track — inserts the clip exactly there.
timeline.align_song.tooltip: For ALL clips on the Display track, clears manual overrides and restores auto-tracking of lyrics/chords (clip = exactly what's on the timeline) — a persistent action, no need to right-click each clip individually.
timeline.fill_gaps.tooltip: Toggle: every clip on the Display track is stretched to the start of the next one, so the display always shows something — the last line stays up until the next one replaces it (a gap between clips otherwise means a blank display). The stretched part is set off inside the clip by a dashed line. Turning it off restores every edge exactly where it was. Saved with the song.
timeline.add_tab.tooltip: Adds a block with an ASCII solo tab (hand-written/pasted text, not derived from individual notes).
timeline.autotime.tooltip: Snaps block starts to the musical grid (bar/beat based on tempo) — no guessing.
timeline.tempo.tooltip: Changes the song's BPM. Optionally rescales existing times proportionally (old tempo / new tempo).
timeline.count_in.tooltip: Inserts/adjusts a count-in before the song — automatically shifts everything else, no manual track shifting.
timeline.snap.tooltip: Snaps dragging to the musical grid (based on song tempo) — not fixed seconds.
timeline.time_label.tooltip: Playhead position — click the ruler or drag the red cursor
help.full.html:
📖 Guitar Pro Viewer & Karaoke Exporter — Help

Open a saved song (Ctrl+O, JSON — the app's own file format) or import a Guitar Pro file (Ctrl+I — tablature/drums/bass, the app never writes back to it), edit the timeline below, save (Ctrl+S).

🖱️ Selecting elements

  • Click = select one element. Shift/Ctrl+click = add/remove from selection.
  • Rubber-band drag (on empty space) = select multiple elements at once — even across MULTIPLE tracks at the same time (lyrics, chords, drums, bass, Display).
  • ] / [ or right-click → "Select from here FORWARD/BACKWARD in time" = select one element and everything matching AFTER/BEFORE it on the SAME track (lyrics+chords together as one group; drums/bass per their own track; Display clips all together, since it's a single master track).
  • "☰ Select Whole Track" (right-click menu) = same as above but in BOTH directions at once — the entire content of that track/kind.
  • Ctrl+A = select absolutely everything on every track at once.

➕ Adding new elements

  • Lyrics / chord: Timeline menu → ＋ Lyric / ＋ Chord.
  • Drums: right-click an empty spot in a specific drum's row → "➕ Add … here". On a completely empty track (no hits yet) a default set of rows (Closed Hi-Hat, Snare, Kick) is offered so there's always something to click.
  • Bass: right-click an empty spot in a string's row → "➕ Add note…", just enter the fret number (bass is never played back — it's a purely visual reference track for aligning with drums/lyrics).
  • Display clip: Ctrl+D (at the playhead, snaps onto a nearby chord-only bar with no clip yet) — or faster: right-click directly on the Display track = clip exactly where you clicked.

📋 Copy, cut, paste

  • Ctrl+C copy / Ctrl+X cut / Ctrl+V paste at the playhead — works on ANY mixed selection (lyrics, chords, drums, bass and Display clips together).
  • The whole copied group is pasted AT ONCE, keeping the original spacing between elements (not each one separately snapped to the grid).
  • Faster: right-click an empty spot on a track (drums/bass/Display) → "📌 Paste Here" — pastes exactly where you clicked.
  • Pasted Display clips detach from auto-follow (they're independent copies now, not a reference to a specific line).
  • The clipboard is shared across all tabs — copy in one song, switch tabs, paste into another (see below).

🗂 Tabs — several songs open at once

  • Each open song = its own tab at the top. New Song (Ctrl+N) and Open… (Ctrl+O) always open a NEW tab — they never overwrite work in progress (exception: a completely empty tab is reused).
  • Import from Guitar Pro (Ctrl+I) targets the ACTIVE tab instead — if it already has lyrics/chords, the GP file is merely added to them (drums + bass), exactly as before.
  • Every tab has its own tempo, undo history, audio and Save target — saving one song never touches another.
  • • before a tab name = unsaved changes. Closing such a tab (the ×) asks Save / Discard / Cancel; so does closing the whole app when several tabs have unsaved work.

↔ Shifting and aligning

  • "↔ Shift Selected…" = an exact, parametric shift of the whole selection by a given number of seconds (equivalent to dragging, but pixel-perfect).
  • "🔄 Re-sync Display" / "🔄🗑 Rebuild Display Track" = refreshes clips on the Display track from the CURRENT lyrics/chords (the latter completely discards and rebuilds from scratch, including deleted/reshuffled lines).

🟣 Display track (what karaoke shows)

The master track at the top — exactly what gets sent to the karaoke display. Double-click a clip = source + display mode. Drag edges = clip length. While a clip auto-follows its content (the default), it always matches what's actually on the timeline; once you drag it manually it detaches and stays independent.

✎ Fixing text and chords

Ctrl+Shift+T — loads the CURRENT lyrics/chords back into the same editor used for importing a new song, lets you fix a mistake (e.g. a missing chord-only bar), and reassembles it. Drums, bass, audio and the Display track stay unchanged — only the lyrics/chords get replaced.

🎵 Audio / waveform

Right-click the waveform = position/stretch (live preview while typing), A/B points for automatic alignment to the drum rhythm. Buttons below the tracks: load MP3/WAV, play, compare against the GP mix.

export.warn_nothing_loaded: First open a Guitar Pro file or JSON.
import.linearize_warn_body:
The GP file contains navigation markers that contradict each other. Measure expansion did not guess — it skipped the disputed jumps and continued linearly, so the song length may not match the score. Check the repeats and the Segno/Coda/Fine markers:
{details}
export.cleanup_note: ⚠ Display track: clips must not overlap (the firmware would never show the later one), so saving shortened {n_short} clips and discarded {n_dropped} (they overlapped a clip with real content and had nothing to show themselves). Undo (Ctrl+Z) reverts this in the editor.
tab.close_confirm_body: “{name}” has unsaved changes. Save before closing the tab?
status.ready: Ready — New Song (Ctrl+N), Open JSON (Ctrl+O), or Import from Guitar Pro (Ctrl+I)
audio.device_combo.tooltip: The audio device the player and test tone play through — Windows "default" may not be what you're actually listening on (e.g. with multiple headphones/Voicemeter connected).
audio.refresh.tooltip: Reload the list of audio devices
audio.test_tone.tooltip: Plays a short beep on the selected device — use THIS to verify you can hear anything at all before troubleshooting the song.
audio.waveform_pos.tooltip: Exact time offset for the recording and ±10% length stretch (to align with a round BPM) — the same as dragging the waveform above the source tracks with the mouse.
audio.auto_align.tooltip: Aligns the recording to the GP drums: finds kick, snare and cymbal hits in the recording and computes the offset + stretch (±10 %) at which most GP hits line up. Without drums in the project it aligns to the tempo grid.
audio.check_duration.tooltip: Purely informational comparison of the computed song length (from tempo/bars) against the actual recording length — changes nothing itself, the verification/decision is yours.
audio.gp_mix.tooltip: Generates/regenerates a synthesized drum sound DIRECTLY from GP data (drums_timeline) and plays it through a second player alongside the real recording — listen to compare what the GP file says against reality. Shares play/pause/stop/shuttle with the recording; volume for each is set separately below. Purely for HUMAN listening verification — nothing is auto-corrected.
audio.bass_mix.tooltip: Generates/regenerates a synthesized bass sound DIRECTLY from GP data (bass_timeline) and plays it through its own player alongside the recording and the GP drum mix — listen to compare what the GP file says against reality. Shares play/pause/stop/shuttle; volume is set separately below. Purely for HUMAN listening verification — nothing is auto-corrected.
audio.bass_mix_not_generated: GP bass mix not generated yet
file.import_midi.tooltip: Import from a standard MIDI file (.mid) — for songs that have no Guitar Pro file. Drums/bass/solo are detected heuristically from the track name; MIDI carries no lyrics or chord symbols — add those by hand or by merging with the web.

help.about.body:
Guitar Pro Viewer & Karaoke Exporter

A Guitar Pro file viewer and karaoke timeline editor that exports to JSON (for the ESP32 karaoke player and others).
web_import.artist_fetch_error: Could not load the artist page: {ex}
web_import.artist_no_links: No song links were found on the page.
web_import.title_new: New Song — text from the web or your own
web_import.tempo_locked.tooltip: Tempo isn't edited here — use "✏️ Tempo…" in the main window so drums and bass get rescaled correctly too.
web_import.count_in_locked.tooltip: A count-in isn't added here — use "🥁⏱ Count-in…" in the main window (this action only changes text and chords).
web_import.ok_btn_edit.tooltip: Closes the dialog and replaces the text/chords in the current song with this corrected version. Drums, bass, the audio link and the Display track stay unchanged.
web_import.steps_edit: Fixing text/chords: edit the lines/chords on the left (or in the middle table)  →  check the JSON preview on the right  →  ✅ Save Text/Chord Fix — replaces ONLY the current song's text and chords, drums/bass/audio/Display stay unchanged.
web_import.steps_new: Full workflow: 1) load text from the web (URL) or just paste/type it directly at the bottom left  →  2) edit the lines/chords (type and content are both editable)  →  3) check the JSON preview on the right  →  ✅ Use in Editor — the song appears right away on the timeline at the current tempo, one line = one time span (a bar).
web_import.tempo.tooltip: Beats per minute — the timeline becomes a regular grid from this: 1 beat = 60/tempo s, 1 bar (4/4) = 4 beats.
web_import.bars_per_line.tooltip: How many bars (4/4) EVERY text line takes — fixed, the same for the whole song, no guessing from syllables. For regular songs (Let It Be…) set it to match the real line length.
web_import.count_in.tooltip: How many bars of silence to insert at the VERY beginning — a gap to click the metronome before the first line.
web_import.left_box_title: 1b) Text  (or type/paste your own directly here — updates live)
web_import.raw_text_placeholder:
Paste or load a chord chart text here:

D          D
Example first line,
D            A7
example second line,
web_import.mid_box_title: 2) Recognized lines  (type and content are both editable)
web_import.right_box_title: 3) What goes into the JSON  (live preview)
web_import.parse_btn.tooltip: Re-parses the text immediately (otherwise it happens automatically as you type).
web_import.artist_btn.tooltip: Enter the artist's page in the URL field (e.g. pisnicky-akordy.cz/olympic) and pick a folder — all songs get downloaded as GP4 + JSON.
web_import.save_btn.tooltip: Optionally also save GP4 + JSON to disk (the dialog stays open).
web_import.ok_btn_new.tooltip: Closes the dialog and loads the song straight onto the timeline (current tempo, one line = one time span).
web_import.status_initial: Enter a URL and load it from the web, or paste/type the text manually at the bottom left.
web_import.counts_status: {verb}: {n_c} chord lines, {n_l} text lines{extra}. Edit line type/content → ✅ Use in Editor.
web_import.preview_empty: (nothing to show yet — paste/edit text on the left)
web_import.nothing_to_use_body: First load text from the web, or paste/type it at the bottom left.
web_import.save_dialog_title: Save GP4 + JSON (enter a base filename)
web_import.need_artist_url_body:
Paste the artist's page into the URL field, e.g.:
https://pisnicky-akordy.cz/olympic
playhead.tooltip: Vertical cursor (playhead) across the whole timeline. Drag with the mouse or click the ruler.
display_clip.tooltip: Display clip — determines what is shown on the display, and from which track, during this section.
bass_lane_bg.tooltip: Bass string {string} — right-click to add a note
menu.add_bass_note_here: Add bass note on string {string} here
drum_row_bg.tooltip: Drum: {drum} — right-click to add a hit
display_lane_bg.tooltip: Display track — right-click to add a clip
properties_panel.title: Properties
properties_panel.placeholder: Select an item on the timeline to edit its properties.
audio.gp_mix_not_generated: GP drum mix not generated yet
dialog.gp_drum_mix_no_data: The GP file has no drum data to generate a mix from.
dialog.gp_bass_mix_no_data: The GP file has no bass data to generate a mix from.
dialog.check_duration_no_audio: Load an MP3/WAV first so there's something to compare against.
dialog.check_duration_result_body:
Computed song end: {computed_end} s @ {bpm} BPM
Actual recording length: {real_dur} s
Deviation: {pct_off} %
dialog.waveform_info: Adjust the recording's offset and stretch relative to the timeline.
dialog.waveform_preview_pending: Load an MP3/WAV first for a preview.
dialog.align_points_too_close_body: Points A and B are too close together in the recording — pick them as far apart as possible (e.g. the start and end of the song) for an accurate result.
dialog.align_stretch_clamped_body: The computed stretch ({stretch} %) is outside the allowed ±10 % range — {stretch_clamped} % was used instead (the closest allowed value). Points A/B probably don't sit on the same bars as the grid — try setting them again.
dialog.auto_align_no_audio_body: Load an MP3/WAV first ("🎵 Load MP3/WAV…") — there's nothing to analyze without a recording.
dialog.auto_align_too_few_onsets_body: Only {n} distinct hits were found — a reliable estimate needs at least 4. Try manual alignment instead (right-click the waveform → point A/B).
dialog.auto_align_summary: Found {n} hits, {matched} of them ({pct} %) fit the grid at this alignment:
dialog.auto_align_low_confidence_warning: ⚠ Low confidence — the recording may not have a steady rhythm, or the project's tempo doesn't match reality. Check the result by listening, or try manual alignment.
waveform.display_gain.tooltip: Waveform drawing gain (does not affect playback volume)
dialog.shift_drum_track_label: Shift in seconds (positive = later, negative = earlier):
dialog.shift_lyrics_track_label: Shift in seconds (positive = later, negative = earlier):
dialog.edit_clip_title: Display clip — what is shown and from where
dialog.auto_time_info:
Snaps text-block starts to the tempo grid (beat/bar).
Lines/chords then sit exactly on the musical grid — no guessing.
dialog.bpm_rescale.tooltip:
Checked: all times (lyrics, chords, drums, bass, clips) are rescaled by the old/new tempo ratio — the existing musical position is preserved.
Unchecked: only the BPM/grid changes, times stay as they are.
dialog.count_in_info: Inserts a few bars of "ticking" (closed hi-hat) before the first note and automatically shifts ALL existing tracks/items by the same amount of time — nothing needs to be moved by hand. During this section the display shows the artist + title and a tempo-based numeric countdown (4, 3, 2, 1…) instead of lyrics/chords.
dialog.paste_at_label: Paste time ({n}× in clipboard, the earliest item lands exactly here):
dialog.auto_align_drums_summary: GP kick and snare hits ({n}) — {pct} % land within ±40 ms of a hit in the recording (median deviation {med} ms).
dialog.auto_align_drift_ok: ✔ The recording keeps tempo — 20 s sections differ by at most {max_ms} ms.
dialog.auto_align_drift_bad: ⚠ The recording does not keep a steady tempo — 20 s sections drift by up to {max_s} s ({examples}). A single offset and stretch cannot align all of it, only on average. Typically a live recording or one without a click track.
dialog.auto_align_drums_low: ⚠ Low match — the recording may not be the same version as the GP file (different structure or tempo). Check by listening.
waveform.drum_legend: hits in recording: ■ kick ■ snare ■ cymbals
timeline.repeats.tooltip: How many times each GP repeat block plays — fixes transcriptions that do not match the recording (e.g. a solo written 2×, played once).
repeats.title: Repeats
repeats.need_gp: Repeats can only be set for a song loaded from Guitar Pro.
repeats.none: The GP file has no repeats.
repeats.info: How many times each repeat block plays. Only the loaded song changes; the GP file on disk stays untouched.
repeats.discard_edits: The song will be rebuilt from GP and manual edits on the timeline will be lost. Continue?
repeats.done: Repeats changed ({n}), song rebuilt from GP.
timeline.fit_tempo.tooltip: For recordings without a click track: finds the start of every bar in the recording from the GP drums and sets a tempo per bar, as the band plays it. Lyrics, chords and drums then match the recording.
fit.title: Fit tempo to recording
fit.need_drums: Fitting needs a GP drum track and at least two bars.
fit.summary:
Bars: {n}. Kick and snare hits within ±40 ms: {before} % with a single offset → {after} % bar by bar. Recording tempo {lo}–{hi} BPM (median {med}). Bar 1 starts in the recording at {start} s.

Once applied, every bar gets its own tempo and the whole timeline is recalculated (undo with Ctrl+Z).
fit.low: ⚠ Low match even bar by bar — the recording may differ from the GP file in structure (repeats, another version). Check Timeline ▸ Repeats… and by listening.
mix_panel.split_ears.tooltip: The recording plays only in the left ear, the GP drum and bass mix only in the right — you can hear who drifts.
